correctness.rationale: The intrinsic multiplication-image cardinality r_n identifies u_n={0,n}: for n≥4 it uniquely has the maximal nonidentity image 2^{n−1}, while for n=2,3 its nonidentity idempotency breaks the tie with {0,1}. Any A with ≥2 positive elements has image at most 2^{n−2}; an earlier singleton {0,k} has a concrete impossible output, establishing strictness. The ideal generated by u_n contains exactly sets with n, and removing n is a monoid isomorphism with T_{n−1}. An automorphism fixes u_n and thus, by induction, fixes its ideal; for any other A, f(A)∪{n}=A∪{n}, and injectivity against the already-fixed ideal forces f(A)=A. Base n1 is trivial. Independently enumerated multiplication-image sizes and intrinsic invariants through n8. The proof—not the eight-case enumeration—establishes the universal classification.
